transcript.text: “Stopped working” can mean a few different faults: a flat battery/charger or power lead issue, a blockage or clogged filter causing an overheat cut-out, or—if the motor still runs—a jammed brush bar or belt problem. First, which of these best describes it: completely dead when switched on; motor runs but there is little/no suction; or motor runs but the brush roller does not spin? If it is cordless, also try charging it in a known-working socket before testing again. If it stopped during use and feels warm, switch it off, remove the battery or unplug it, clear the bin and any obvious blockage, then leave it to cool fully before retrying. A thermal cut-out can reset once cool, but repeated cut-outs usually point to restricted airflow or a failing motor.
its completely dead when i switch it on. its a corded one, the red Henry. stopped while i was doing the stairs

Because it is completely dead and stopped during use, start with the supply and an overheat cut-out. The most likely causes are a plug fuse/cable issue, or a thermal cut-out from a blockage; the switch or motor are less likely until those are ruled out. 1. Unplug it. Try the wall socket with another appliance you know works. If the socket is dead, the vacuum may be fine. 2. Check the plug and full length of the cable, especially where it enters the plug and the vacuum, for cuts, crushing or a loose connection. Do not use it if the cable or plug is damaged. If the plug has a fuse, replace it only with the same rating marked on it/inside the plug (commonly 13A). 3. As it stopped while working, leave it unplugged for at least an hour. While it is off, empty the bag/bin if applicable and check the hose, wand, floor head and filters for an obvious blockage. A restriction can overheat the motor and trip its safety cut-out. Then try it again in the known-working socket. If it remains totally dead with a sound plug fuse and undamaged lead, it is likely an internal switch, cable-reel connection or motor fault, which is an engineer repair rather than a safe DIY internal repair.

the lamp works in the socket so thats ok. theres black tape round the wire near the plug, my son did it ages ago, and its a bit bent there. it came on for a second once when i moved the wire then went off again. i havent got a screwdriver or spare fuse

The taped, bent cable near the plug is the overwhelmingly likely fault. Coming on briefly when that section is moved is typical of a broken wire or poor connection inside the flex/plug, not an overheating blockage. Stop using it and leave it unplugged. Tape is not a safe repair for a mains cable, particularly where the copper cores may be broken or insulation damaged; moving it can cause a shock, overheating or arcing. It needs the plug and cable end inspected and repaired/replaced by a competent appliance repairer or electrician. They can also check the plug fuse at the same time. As you have no screwdriver or spare fuse, do not attempt to open the plug or improvise a repair. An internal switch or cable-reel fault is possible, but the response when the damaged lead is moved makes the lead/plug connection much more likely.

Brush bar jam or belt fault (low)
